# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Jul 20, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on critical infrastructure updates, including standardizing Dockerfiles to Chainguard `wolfi-base` and remediating security vulnerabilities by bumping various dependencies. Several long-standing issues were also closed, addressing Kona-node parity and super-root migration runbooks.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Infrastructure Security and Standardization
Significant efforts were made to enhance the security and consistency of the infrastructure. All `infra` service Dockerfiles were standardized to use Chainguard `wolfi-base`, replacing older base images for improved security and maintainability ([#671](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/671)). Additionally, vulnerable dependencies across Go modules, Yarn workspaces, and Poetry projects were updated to remediate flagged CVEs ([#670](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/670)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Kona-node Feature Parity and Bug Resolution
The issue regarding the implementation of `syncmode.offset-el-safe` for Kona-node was closed ([#21243](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21243)). It was determined that Kona-node does not exhibit the bug this flag fixes in op-node, and its existing safety mechanisms are arguably more conservative. The issue concerning `TestSequencerPreset` not supporting the Kona sequencer was also closed, as it is likely outdated after recent monorepo updates ([#18675](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18675)).

### Super-root Migration Runbook Fixes
The issue related to fixing super-root migration runbooks for simplified `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` was closed ([#21709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21709)). This indicates that the runbooks have been updated to reflect the current fault-game behavior.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were reported today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### op-geth Decoupling: L2 Transaction Representation and Client Updates
Discussions on [#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20264) (opgeth-decoupling: make op-service/sources the OP-aware eth client) revealed a design correction for the `op-batcher` migration. It was determined that `op-batcher` cannot migrate to `InfoAndUserTxs` and will instead use `PayloadByNumber` to fetch `*eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope`. This is because `InfoAndUserTxs` drops critical information required for batch building, such as the L1-info deposit transaction and post-exec transactions. The partitioned accessors (`InfoAndUserTxs`, `InfoAndDeposits`, `InfoAndFirstDeposit`) will still be added for test migrations. Further complexities were noted regarding `optypes.Receipts` root derivation, which requires handling three distinct OP arms (post-Canyon deposit receipts, pre-Canyon deposit receipts, and `0x7D` post-exec receipts), and `FetchReceipts` needing to derive transaction hashes from raw transactions.

### op-geth Decoupling: Call-site Swaps and Transition Scaffolding
Regarding [#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20263) (opgeth-decoupling: swap call-sites to op-core/* across op-node, op-service, op-batcher), it was noted that all three sub-issues are closed, and the remaining scope is tracked in [#21901](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21901). A key point from earlier discussions highlighted that `optypes` helpers like `IsDepositTx(tx)` are transition scaffolding, operating on `*types.Transaction` from op-geth. These helpers are temporary and will be removed at the final cutover, serving to decouple call sites from op-geth internals before the L2 transaction representation changes. Developers are advised to prefer decoding to `optypes.DepositTx` directly when possible, rather than building new long-lived APIs on these temporary helpers.

### Flaky Test: reth-optimism-node integration test SIGSEGV
The ongoing investigation into [#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20973) (flake: reth-optimism-node integration test peers_negotiate_eth_69 SIGSEGVs on teardown) received a detailed update. An independent review refuted the earlier hypothesis that the segfault was caused by a detached payload thread polling a torn-down runtime. Experimental verification showed that the `select(on_shutdown, task)` wrapper prevents polling a dead runtime, and `payload-builder` threads are gone before `exit_group`. The "own-runtime patch" is not being pursued as a fix because it doesn't change behavior at runtime death. The actual mechanism of the segfault remains unidentified, but potential culprits include `mdbx_env_close_ex` not being called, detached `engine` and `persistence` threads, or RocksDB background threads racing with C++ static destructors. The recommended next step is to capture a core dump/faulting stack in CI to pinpoint the exact cause.

### Flaky Test: TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement
For [#21635](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21635) (flaky test: `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`), a root cause and fix update were provided. The flake is caused by `FollowSource` canonicalizing upstream block N+1 while the light sequencer still has a timer armed against block N. This can lead to the timer running first and emitting a build start on the removed parent N, causing `missing parent header` and `Invalid payload attributes` errors in op-reth, leading to a critical shutdown. The flakiness stems from the Go `select` ordering. The proposed fix involves rejecting non-derived build starts unless their parent block ID matches the engine controller's current unsafe block ID, with the check and follow-source sharing the controller mutex to prevent stale Engine API calls. Verification with focused regressions showed the fix to be effective.
